The test image shows:
- Stem base with dense white cottony/fluffy mycelium radiating outward
- Small spherical yellowish/tan sclerotia scattered around the infected area
- Brown decayed stem tissue underneath

This pattern strongly suggests **Southern_Blight** (white mycelium + mustard-seed sized sclerotia at stem base). Let me verify with reference images across 4 classes.

**Analysis summary:**

- **Test image**: Stem base infection with dense white fluffy/cottony mycelium radiating outward, and numerous small spherical yellowish/tan sclerotia (mustard-seed sized) scattered on the surface.

- **Southern_Blight** (stem ref): Shows bleached stem lesion — a different stage of same disease. The white mycelium + small sclerotia pattern matches the KB description perfectly: "white fungal mats (mycelia) radiating from infected tissue... spherical sclerotia ranging in color from light tan to dark reddish-brown."

- **Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot** (stem ref): Large, irregular, dark grayish-black sclerotia embedded inside the stem tissue — clearly different from the small round yellowish sclerotia in the test image.

- **Rhizopus_Soft_Rots** (stem ref): Microscopic dark sporangia on stalks — entirely different morphology.

The white cottony mycelium + small round tan sclerotia at the stem base is the classic hallmark of Southern Blight (*Sclerotium rolfsii*), not Sclerotinia (which has large dark embedded sclerotia) or any other candidate.
